name: MathlibAnnex.SeminormBall.measure_lt
title: A compact proper subset of a seminorm ball has smaller Haar measure

content.display_title: A compact proper subset of a seminorm ball has smaller Haar measure
content.one_sentence_role: Finds a nonempty open part of the missing set and uses finiteness of the compact set to make the measure comparison strict.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $E$ be a real normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let $\mu$ be an additive Haar measure, and let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm. Put $B_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$. If $K\subsetneq B_p$ is compact, then

$$\mu(K)<\mu(B_p).$$
content.assumptions: The measure is an additive Haar measure: in particular it is finite on compact sets and positive on nonempty open sets. The seminorm $p$ is continuous for the given norm topology; it need not be definite. The set $K$ is compact, is contained in $B_p$, and is not equal to $B_p$. No convexity of $K$, finite-dimensionality of $E$, or finiteness of $\mu(B_p)$ is added.
content.conclusion: The measure inequality is strict in the extended nonnegative reals $[0,\infty]$. Compactness ensures $\mu(K)<\infty$, while $\mu(B_p)$ is allowed to be infinite.
content.proof_summary:
Choose $y\in B_p\setminus K$. Compactness makes $K$ closed, so its complement contains a neighbourhood of $y$. An inward point $ty$ with $0<t<1$ sufficiently close to $1$ remains outside $K$. By seminorm homogeneity,

$$p(ty)=t\,p(y)\le t<1.$$

Continuity of $p$ therefore makes $\{z:p(z)<1\}\cap K^c$ a nonempty open subset of $B_p\setminus K$. Positivity of Haar measure on nonempty open sets implies $0<\mu(B_p\setminus K)$. The sets $K$ and $B_p\setminus K$ are measurable and disjoint, with union $B_p$. Hence

$$\mu(B_p)=\mu(K)+\mu(B_p\setminus K)>\mu(K),$$

where strictness uses $\mu(K)<\infty$, obtained from compactness. This reasoning remains valid if the second summand is infinite.

proof_steps.text:
To make the inward choice explicit, take $\delta>0$ with the open norm ball of radius $\delta$ about $y$ contained in $K^c$. Set

$$a=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{\delta}{2(\|y\|+1)}\right\},\qquad t=1-a.$$

Then $0<a\le1/2$, so $0<t<1$, and

$$\|ty-y\|=a\|y\|<\frac\delta2<\delta.$$

Thus $ty\notin K$. The strict inequality for $p(ty)$ supplies an interior point of $B_p$; intersecting its open neighbourhood with $K^c$ gives the nonempty open defect.

The compact set $K$ is closed and Borel measurable. Continuity of $p$ makes $B_p=\{p\le1\}$ closed and hence measurable, so its difference with $K$ is measurable. The containment $K\subseteq B_p$ gives the disjoint decomposition $B_p=K\cup(B_p\setminus K)$. Additivity and the finite compact measure now justify the strict inequality, without subtracting infinite measures.

content.lean_realization_notes: The key geometric input is a nonempty interior of $B_p\setminus K$. It concerns the ambient norm topology, even when $p$ has a kernel. Taking $p=\|\cdot\|$ gives the separately cited norm-ball specialization, without imposing convexity on $K$.
